prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I’m sorry you were in an accident — that’s stressful. I can’t pick a single “best” lawyer for you, but I can help you find the right one and tell you what to look for. A few quick priorities first, then how to choose and what to ask at a consultation.

Immediate steps (if you haven’t already)
- Get medical care now and follow all treatment. Your health and the medical record are crucial.
- Preserve evidence: photos of vehicles, scene, injuries; contact info for witnesses; police report number.
- Don’t give a recorded statement to the other driver’s insurer without talking to a lawyer.
- Avoid posting details or photos of the accident or injuries on social media.
- Note deadlines: in California the statute of limitations for most personal injury claims is 2 years from the date of injury (act quickly).

What kind of lawyer you should hire
- A personal injury attorney who focuses on auto accidents and has trial experience. Look for someone who handles similar cases (car, motorcycle, pedestrian, etc.) regularly.
- If catastrophic injury or complex insurance issues (UM/UIM, commercial vehicle, rideshare), consider a lawyer who advertises those specialties.

How to find and narrow candidates
- Use local resources: Alameda County Bar Association lawyer referral, State Bar of California website (to check licenses/discipline), and local Google/Avvo/Martindale-Hubbell reviews.
- Ask friends/family for referrals, or post in local neighborhood groups for recommendations.
- Look for lawyers who handle cases in Alameda/Contra Costa County and are familiar with Pleasanton area courts and medical providers.

Important factors to compare
- Experience with car-accident cases and specific injury types (e.g., neck/back, fractures, spinal cord, TBI).
- Track record: settlements and verdicts, trial experience.
- Who will handle your case (the named attorney vs. junior staff).
- Communication style and availability (how often you’ll hear from them).
- Fee structure and costs (contingency fees are standard; typical ranges and who advances costs).
- Reputation for honesty and client care (reviews, references).

Questions to ask at the free consultation
- How many auto-accident personal injury cases have you handled?
- What percentage of your cases settle vs go to trial?
- Who specifically will handle my case day-to-day?
- What is your contingency fee? How are costs handled if we don’t recover?
- What’s a realistic timeline and expected range of value for a case like mine?
- Do you have experience with my injuries and with my insurer(s)?
- Can you provide references from recent clients?
- Will you advance medical lien payments or work with medical providers for treatment now?

Typical fees and costs
- Most personal injury lawyers work on contingency (you pay only if they recover). Standard contingency fees: ~33% if settled before suit; 33–40% if suit/trial (varies). Clarify costs (filing fees, expert fees) and whether the attorney advances them.

Red flags
- Guarantees of a large settlement or pressuring you to sign immediately.
- Poor communication or evasive answers on who will handle the case.
- No office or no verifiable track record.

Local next steps I can do for you
- If you’d like, I can: 
  - Search for several Pleasanton/tri‑valley personal injury attorneys and provide short profiles and links to reviews; or
  - Help you prepare for consultations (a short checklist or script); or
  - Evaluate options if you already have a couple of names.

If you want specific recommendations, tell me:
- The date of the accident, brief facts (who was at fault, injuries, whether police/ambulance were involved),
- Whether you’ve seen a doctor yet,
- Any insurers involved,
- Any preferences (female attorney, trial lawyer, bilingual).
